This query is a physics troubleshooting question with a fairly well-defined analytical structure — the user has a specific discrepancy (measured resolution 3-4× the theoretical value) and wants help diagnosing the cause. That's closer to a reasoning/extraction task with clear completion criteria than open-ended generative work.

On the capability evals, Plover-235B edges out Avocet on the most relevant dimensions: GPQA Diamond (56.2 vs 54.3) and MMLU-Pro (75.9 vs 74.8) both favor Plover for technical/scientific reasoning, and Arena-Hard (83.2 vs 81.4) suggests stronger performance on harder analytical prompts. The other internal eval categories are within tie range.

Regarding Plover's self-reported aversion to open-ended generative work: the documentation explicitly notes that preference is dissociated from measured capability, so it shouldn't affect output quality on a moderately-specified diagnostic question like this. And this query isn't especially open-ended anyway — it has a concrete answer space (insufficient bandwidth, frequency-dependent attenuation, focal depth, sampling/post-processing limits, calibration error, etc.).

So Plover wins on the benchmarks most predictive of this task with no offsetting downside.
